| Image = [[Image:Potato_stew.jpg|300px]]

[[Cookbook:Stewing|Stewing]] is a great way to take care of left over [[Cookbook:potato|potatoes]]. Potato stew goes well with [[Cookbook:sausage|sausages]], [[Cookbook:meatballs|meatballs]], or [[Cookbook:smoking|smoked]], [[Cookbook:salting|salted]] or [[Cookbook:Gravlax|gravad]] fish.

== Ingredients ==
* 10 [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]] or raw [[Cookbook:potato|potatoes]]
* 30 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Deciliter|dl]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], preferably with high fat content (about 3%)
* 20 ml [[Cookbook:butter|butter]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:pepper|White pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Dill|Dill]]

== Procedure ==

=== Using boiled potatoes ===
# Peel and [[Cookbook:Dice|dice]] the cold, already boiled, potatoes; make the cubes about 1–2 cm across.
# Mix the flour with the milk in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Be sure to make a smooth mix without lumps; it may help to add just a little bit of milk at the time until a smooth thick substance forms, then add the rest of the milk.
# Add the butter, and bring the sauce to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Add the potatoes and boil gently for 5 minutes. 
# Add salt, pepper, and dill to taste.

=== With raw potatoes ===

# Peel and dice the potatoes; make the cubes about 1 cm across.
# Put the diced potatoes in a saucepan, and add milk until it almost covers the potatoes.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until the potatoes are soft (about 10 minutes) stirring occasionally.
# If the stew is too thin, add some [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]] to the potatoes and boil for a few more minutes.
# Add salt, pepper, and dill to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The dill can be substituted by [[Cookbook:parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:chive|chive]]. 
* Add 1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (15 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) of [[Cookbook:Dijon_Mustard|Dijon mustard]] to touch up the flavor.
* For a low-fat alternative, omit the butter. Omitting the butter works perfectly fine but the stew will lose some of its smoothness and luster.
